title: Champagne Tarragon Scallop Skewers
seoTitle: Champagne Tarragon Scallop Skewers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Scallop skewer night—restaurant shellfish on the hall grill in minutes
subtitle: Charred sea scallops, shallot-tarragon butter, and lemon for ten
description: Large sea scallops thread onto skewers, grill until caramelized and 125°F, and finish with sizzling garlic-lemon butter and fresh parsley.

steps.title: Prep scallops
steps.instruction: Remove side muscle from each scallop. Pat completely dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build garlic butter
steps.instruction: Melt butter with garlic over low heat 3 minutes. Off heat, add lemon juice and zest. Keep warm, not boiling. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat grill hot
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to high, 450°F. Oil grates generously—wet scallops stick. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Skewer scallops
steps.instruction: Thread 3–4 scallops per skewer with small gaps. Brush lightly with grapeseed oil. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill scallops
steps.instruction: Grill skewers 2 minutes per side until golden crust forms and centers read 120–125°F. Do not overcook. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brief rest
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 2 minutes off heat. Scallops carry to 125°F. Transfer to hotel pans. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Butter at service
steps.instruction: Spoon warm garlic butter over scallops at the line. Scatter parsley. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes max. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve 4 scallops per firefighter with bread for soaking butter. Call it fast—scallops wait poorly. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Dry scallops are non-negotiable—moisture prevents the sear.
Two minutes per side max; rubber scallops mean the grill was too slow or too long.
Garlic butter at the line keeps scallops from steaming under foil.
tonightSpread: Garlic butter scallop skewers with crusty bread.
Simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette.
leftovers: Chop scallops into seafood pasta with extra butter.
Flake into breakfast hash with potatoes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Scallops cook faster than any protein on the line. They need a brief hold at 140°F max—perfect for a quick special meal between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Pat scallops completely dry. Grill high 450°F—2 minutes per side max. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes only. Garlic butter at service, not during hold.
